0._section_summary: The abstract describes a single (unnamed) study that examined how cognitive fusion and body appreciation relate to the association between body image discrepancy and disordered eating in a sample of 369 women, controlling for BMI. Results indicate greater body image discrepancy is associated with more disordered eating, and this relationship is partially mediated by higher cognitive fusion related to body image and lower body appreciation. The abstract does not report participant demographics (country, age, race), recruitment source, measurement instruments (BAS/BAS-2), BMI values, or correlations between body appreciation and BMI.

1._section_summary: This abstract reports a single study with a sample of 369 women that examined how cognitive fusion and body appreciation relate to the link between perceived discrepancy between actual and ideal body and disordered eating, controlling for BMI. Results indicate that greater perceived discrepancy is associated with more disordered eating, and this relation is partly explained by higher cognitive fusion regarding appearance and lower body appreciation.

6._section_summary: This section reports a single path analysis testing how body image-related cognitive fusion (CFQ_BI) and body appreciation (BAS_2) mediate the relationship between body image discrepancy (BID) and disordered eating (EDE_Q), controlling for BMI. The final model (Figure 1) explained 13% of CFQ_BI variance, 23% of BAS_2 variance, and 67% of EDE_Q variance; all reported path coefficients were significant and BMI had only a small direct effect on EDE_Q. No explicit labels like 'Study 1' or multiple separate studies/subsamples are mentioned in this section.
